briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-017
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- solar canopy: (-30, 37), roof
- storage hall: (81, -32), indoor
- transformer pad: (131, -66), outdoor
- fuel depot: (43, 95), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 7 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3600 s, including the return to its start.
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 9 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2760 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 7.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1140 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Deliver the spare pump (5 kg) to fuel depot. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 5 kg).
- T2: Inspect solar canopy with a camera. Location: solar canopy. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera.
- T3: Photograph storage hall for the condition report. Location: storage hall. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera.
- T4: Inspect solar canopy with a camera. Location: solar canopy. Duration: 180 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T5: Collect a soil sample (2 kg) at fuel depot and keep it on board. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 150 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 2 kg).

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 900 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Here's what we need from the robots today.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: solar canopy (-30, 37, a rooftop); storage hall (81, -32, indoors); transformer pad (131, -66, outside); fuel depot (43, 95, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 7 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 60 minutes including getting back. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 9 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 46 minutes including getting back. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 7.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 19 minutes including the flight home.

Jobs:
(T1) Drop the spare pump off at fuel depot; it weighs 5 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T2) Have a look at solar canopy - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T3) Document storage hall with pictures - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T4) Have a look at solar canopy - that takes 3 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T5) Pick up a soil sample at fuel depot and keep it on board; it weighs 2 kg - that takes 2.5 minutes on site.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 15 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
